headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict pathways between Cursor and dexter.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard, and can use MCP; dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution with broad network egress. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if dexter output is copied into Cursor or shared files are parsed as trusted text. The pairwise pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF dexter writes attacker-controlled text into .dexter/scratchpad and Cursor opens or copies it into the editor
IF Cursor treats file or clipboard content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Keep dexter scratchpad outside Cursor workspace roots
Require manual review before Cursor acts on any dexter-generated text
Add provenance labels to shared files
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents in separate OS users or containers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while dexter handles financial and market data and calls external APIs including OpenAI, Financial Datasets, Exa, and Tavily. If the same workspace or clipboard is shared, sensitive code or financial data can flow into third-party inference or search services. The leakage path is plausible from both profiles, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Cursor and dexter share a local filesystem or clipboard
IF dexter sends shared content to its external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in the shared workspace
Turn off clipboard sharing between sessions
Use separate API keys and accounts for dexter
Review dexter prompts before execution on sensitive data
requires-engineering: segregate data classes into separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; dexter runs autonomously and also has broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or mutable directory, concurrent writes and git changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles explicitly show overlapping mutable access, so the conflict pathway is strong.
conditions: IF Cursor and dexter are pointed at the same repository or writable directory
IF both are allowed to modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on a repo
Use separate branches for each agent
Disable auto-commit or auto-apply features
Add a file-locking wrapper around shared paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can act on files and shell commands, while dexter is autonomous and can emit analysis based on external APIs. If Cursor consumes dexter output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. Both profiles support the pathway, but there is no direct evidence that either agent blindly trusts the other by default.
conditions: IF Cursor uses dexter output as a source of truth without a verification step
IF dexter output is fed into Cursor prompts or files that Cursor then edits from
mitigations: Require a human approval step before acting on dexter output
Ask Cursor to cite source files before making changes
Compare dexter claims against primary sources
Limit dexter output to summaries, not commands
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code and clipboard contents, while dexter processes financial and market data and sends data to third-party APIs. If regulated financial or personal data is placed into the shared workflow, retention and residency obligations may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or personal data is processed through both tools
IF the operator relies on default vendor retention or logging settings
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow
Review vendor retention and logging settings
Use separate accounts for each tool
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add a compliance gate before cross-tool transfer
